modern: How cruel it is not to allow men to strive after the things which seem to them suitable to their nature and profitable! And yet in a way you do not allow them to do this when you are annoyed because they do wrong. For they are certainly drawn towards things because they suppose them to be suitable to their nature and profitable to them. But it is not so. Teach them, then, and show them, without being angry.

explained.summary: People do wrong because they’re chasing what they believe is good for them. They’re mistaken, but that’s their motive. So when you’re angry at them, you’re in a sense denying them the right to pursue what they think will help them, which is harsh. Better to teach them and show them the truth, without anger.
explained.today: The teenager who lies to get out of trouble, or the colleague who cuts a corner, thinks they’re doing the sensible thing. Explaining calmly why it isn’t will do more good than an outburst.
